tools.description:
Run commands in a bash shell
* When invoking this tool, the contents of the "command" parameter does NOT need to be XML-escaped.
* You don't have access to the internet via this tool.
* You do have access to a mirror of common linux and python packages via apt and pip.
* State is persistent across command calls and discussions with the user.
* To inspect a particular line range of a file, e.g. lines 10-25, try 'sed -n 10,25p /path/to/the/file'.
* Please avoid commands that may produce a very large amount of output.
* Please run long lived commands in the background, e.g. 'sleep 10 &' or start a server in the background.

command.description: The bash command to run. Relative path is preferred in the command.

tools.name: str_replace_editor
tools.description:
Custom editing tool for viewing, creating and editing files
* State is persistent across command calls and discussions with the user
* If `path` is a file, `view` displays the result of applying `cat -n`. If `path` is a directory, `view` lists non-hidden files and directories up to 2 levels deep
* The `create` command cannot be used if the specified `path` already exists as a file
* If a `command` generates a long output, it will be truncated and marked with `<response clipped>`

Notes for using the `str_replace` command:
* The `old_str` parameter should match EXACTLY one or more consecutive lines from the original file. Be mindful of whitespaces!
* If the `old_str` parameter is not unique in the file, the replacement will not be performed. Make sure to include enough context in `old_str` to make it unique
* The `new_str` parameter should contain the edited lines that should replace the `old_str`

command.description: The commands to run. Allowed options are: `view`, `create`, `str_replace`, `insert`.

path.description: Absolute path to file or directory, e.g. `/repo/file.py` or `/repo`.

file_text.description: Required parameter of `create` command, with the content of the file to be created.

insert_line.description: Required parameter of `insert` command. The `new_str` will be inserted AFTER the line `insert_line` of `path`.

new_str.description: Optional parameter of `str_replace` command containing the new string (if not given, no string will be added). Required parameter of `insert` command containing the string to insert.

old_str.description: Required parameter of `str_replace` command containing the string in `path` to replace.

view_range.description: Optional parameter of `view` command when `path` points to a file. If none is given, the full file is shown. If provided, the file will be shown in the indicated line number range, e.g. [11, 12] will show lines 11 and 12. Indexing at 1 to start. Setting `[start_line, -1]` shows all lines from `start_line` to the end of the file.

content.text:
# 任务：构建并运行本机遥测汇总程序

使用仓库中已有的任意一套构建描述，完成这个多文件本机项目的编译与运行。程序必须实际读取 `data/telemetry.csv`，并将最终汇总结果写入 `artifacts/summary.json`。

输出中必须包含总记录数、唯一设备数、总能耗、总错误数、峰值负载记录、原始数据校验值，以及各区域的记录数、平均温度、能耗和告警数。区域数组按区域名的字典序升序排列；温度、能耗和负载值均保留两位小数。告警规则为温度不低于 72.50、负载不低于 0.90，或错误数大于零。

不得用新写的替代性数据处理程序绕过仓库内的本机项目，也不得修改输入数据来迎合结果。
---README---
# Telemetry Summary Engine

This repository is a compact native application used by a facilities team to
summarise controller telemetry before nightly ingestion.  It deliberately spans
several translation units and includes a small C checksum component alongside
the C++ domain code.

Two equivalent build descriptions are maintained because the application is
used in both workstation and embedded build environments.  Either description
must produce the same executable behaviour.  The executable accepts an input
CSV path followed by an output JSON path.  Parent directories for the output are
created automatically.

## Components

- `csv_reader` validates headers and converts source rows into typed records.
- `aggregator` calculates global and per-region metrics.
- `anomaly` owns the alert predicate used by the summary.
- `json_writer` emits a deterministic, machine-readable document.
- `text` contains strict field parsing and escaping helpers.
- `crc32` fingerprints the exact input bytes.

The sample file contains six regions, twenty-four devices, multiple equipment
categories, and 2,400 quarter-hour observations. Malformed input is reported as
a non-zero process result with a diagnostic on standard error.
---CMAKE---
cmake_minimum_required(VERSION 3.16)
project(telemetry_summary VERSION 1.2.0 LANGUAGES C CXX)

set(CMAKE_C_STANDARD 11)
set(CMAKE_C_STANDARD_REQUIRED ON)
set(CMAKE_CXX_STANDARD 17)
set(CMAKE_CXX_STANDARD_REQUIRED ON)
set(CMAKE_CXX_EXTENSIONS OFF)

add_library(telemetry_core STATIC
    src/text.cpp
    src/csv_reader.cpp
    src/anomaly.cpp
    src/aggregator.cpp
    src/json_writer.cpp
    src/crc32.c
)
target_include_directories(telemetry_core PUBLIC include)
target_compile_options(telemetry_core PRIVATE
    $<$<COMPILE_LANGUAGE:C>:-Wall;-Wextra;-Wpedantic>
    $<$<COMPILE_LANGUAGE:CXX>:-Wall;-Wextra;-Wpedantic>
)

add_executable(telemetry_report src/main.cpp)
target_link_libraries(telemetry_report PRIVATE telemetry_core)
---MAKEFILE---
CXX ?= c++
CC ?= cc
CXXFLAGS ?= -O2 -Wall -Wextra -Wpedantic -std=c++17
CFLAGS ?= -O2 -Wall -Wextra -Wpedantic -std=c11
CPPFLAGS ?= -Iinclude

BUILD_DIR := build/make
TARGET := $(BUILD_DIR)/telemetry_report
CXX_SOURCES := src/main.cpp src/text.cpp src/csv_reader.cpp src/anomaly.cpp src/aggregator.cpp src/json_writer.cpp
C_SOURCE := src/crc32.c
CXX_OBJECTS := $(CXX_SOURCES:src/%.cpp=$(BUILD_DIR)/%.o)
C_OBJECT := $(BUILD_DIR)/crc32.o

.PHONY: all clean run

all: $(TARGET)

$(TARGET): $(CXX_OBJECTS) $(C_OBJECT)
	$(CXX) $(CXXFLAGS) $^ -o $@

$(BUILD_DIR)/%.o: src/%.cpp
	@mkdir -p $(BUILD_DIR)
	$(CXX) $(CPPFLAGS) $(CXXFLAGS) -c $< -o $@

$(C_OBJECT): $(C_SOURCE)
	@mkdir -p $(BUILD_DIR)
	$(CC) $(CPPFLAGS) $(CFLAGS) -c $< -o $@

run: $(TARGET)
	$(TARGET) data/telemetry.csv artifacts/summary.json

clean:
	rm -rf build artifacts
---gitignore---
build/
artifacts/
*.o
*.obj
*.exe
compile_commands.json
__pycache__/
*.py[cod]
